title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations Establish the Molecular Basis for the Broad Allostery Hotspot Distributions in the Tetracycline Repressor.
authors: Yuan, Yuchen; Deng, Jiahua; Cui, Qiang
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟研究四环素阻遏蛋白（TetR）中配体与DNA结合位点间的别构偶联机制，虽非直接聚焦TF-DNA特异性结合识别，但属于蛋白-DNA互作体系且采用物理模拟方法，对TF-DNA动态结合机理建模有方法学借鉴价值。
abstract: It is imperative to identify the network of residues essential to the allosteric coupling for the purpose of rationally engineering allostery in proteins. Deep mutational scanning analysis has emerged as a function-centric approach for identifying such allostery hotspots in a comprehensive and unbiased fashion, leading to observations that challenge our understanding of allostery at the molecular level. Specifically, a recent deep mutational scanning study of the tetracycline repressor (TetR) revealed an unexpectedly broad distribution of allostery hotspots throughout the protein structure. Using extensive molecular dynamics simulations (up to 50 mus) and free energy computations, we establish the molecular and energetic basis for the strong anticooperativity between the ligand and DNA binding sites. The computed free energy landscapes in different ligation states illustrate that allostery in TetR is well described by a conformational selection model, in which the apo state samples a broad set of conformations, and specific ones are selectively stabilized by either ligand or DNA binding. By examining a range of structural and dynamic properties of residues at both local and global scales, we observe that various analyses capture different subsets of experimentally identified hotspots, suggesting that these residues modulate allostery in distinct ways. These results motivate the development of a thermodynamic model that qualitatively explains the broad distribution of hotspot residues and their distinct features in molecular dynamics simulations. The multifaceted strategy that we establish here for hotspot evaluations and our insights into their mechanistic contributions are useful for modulating protein allostery in mechanistic and engineering studies.
abstract_zh: 为了合理设计蛋白质中的别构调控，必须识别对别构偶联至关重要的残基网络。深度突变扫描分析已成为一种以功能为中心的方法，用于全面且无偏地识别此类别构热点，从而产生了挑战我们在分子水平上对别构理解的现象。具体而言，最近一项针对四环素阻遏蛋白（TetR）的深度突变扫描研究揭示了别构热点在蛋白质结构中出乎意料的广泛分布。通过使用广泛的分子动力学模拟（长达50微秒）和自由能计算，我们建立了配体与DNA结合位点之间强负协同性的分子和能量基础。不同配体状态下的计算自由能景观表明，TetR中的别构现象可通过构象选择模型很好地描述，其中脱辅基状态采样广泛的构象集合，而特定构象则被配体或DNA结合选择性稳定。通过检查残基在局部和全局尺度上的多种结构和动态特性，我们观察到不同分析捕获了实验识别热点的不同子集，表明这些残基以不同方式调节别构。这些结果促使我们开发了一个热力学模型，该模型定性地解释了热点残基的广泛分布及其在分子动力学模拟中的独特特征。我们在此建立的多方面热点评估策略及其对机制贡献的见解，对于在机制和工程研究中调节蛋白质别构具有实用价值。
